summary: Post-repair DHCP lease collision causes Autopilot enrollment to time out on depot-rebuilt Precision workstations
description:
Issue summary:
After SSD replacement and depot reimage, a small cohort (~6) of Dell Precision 5580 units fail Autopilot/Intune enrollment during the initial provisioning step. Devices boot, fetch image, and reach 'applying provisioning' but stall waiting for network-based SCEP and MDM enrollment. Enrollment ultimately times out and image is marked as failed.

Impact:
- Blocking provisioning for replacement/repair fleet arriving from depot (affects 6 machines reported so far).
- Delays RMA turnaround; customers waiting on devices.
- Manual remediation currently required (DHCP lease purge + reimage) which takes ~30 minutes per device.

Environment:
- Production provisioning image (autopilot + corp preprovisioned).
- Region: us-west-2 corporate DHCP on-prem site.
- Affected hardware: Dell Precision 5580 with NVMe SSD swapped during depot repair.

Steps to reproduce (observed flow):
1) Depot performs SSD replacement and runs depot reimage (corporate imaging flow).
2) Device boots into provisioning image; systemd-networkd brings up link.
3) DHCP client obtains lease, but provisioning agent later reports ‘network unreachable’ when connecting to SCEP and enrollment endpoints.
4) Enrollment retries until timeout; imaging marked as failed.

Observed behavior / key logs:
- journalctl excerpt from repro unit (truncated):
  Mar 08 10:12:31 precision5580 systemd-networkd[812]: eth0: Gained carrier
  Mar 08 10:12:31 precision5580 dhclient[940]: DHCPREQUEST on eth0 to 10.0.0.2 port 67
  Mar 08 10:12:31 precision5580 dhclient[940]: DHCPACK from 10.0.0.2
  Mar 08 10:13:03 provision-agent[1221]: ERROR connecting to scep.redwood.internal: connect ECONNREFUSED
  Mar 08 10:13:03 provision-agent[1221]: retrying (attempt 3/5)
  Mar 08 10:13:33 kernel: r8169 0000:03:00.0 eth0: MAC address changed from 3c:97:0e:aa:bb:cc to 3c:97:0e:dd:ee:ff
  Mar 08 10:13:33 systemd-networkd[812]: eth0: link lost
  Mar 08 10:13:34 systemd-networkd[812]: eth0: Gained carrier
  Mar 08 10:13:34 dhclient[940]: DHCPDISCOVER on eth0 to 255.255.255.255 port 67
  Mar 08 10:13:34 dhclient[940]: DHCPACK from 10.0.0.2 (lease offered for 86400 seconds)

- On DHCP server (ISC DHCP) logs there are duplicate lease entries for the old MAC and the new MAC from the same scope; server served a lease but client traffic observed on a different VLAN/gateway for a subset of packets (packet capture showed mismatched gateway).

Expected behavior:
- After depot repair and reimage, device should successfully request and maintain a DHCP lease, reach SCEP/MDM endpoints, and complete Autopilot enrollment without manual intervention.

Additional notes:
- Not all depot-rebuilt units are affected; pattern correlates to units that also had EC firmware updated at depot (suggests transient NIC firmware or EC interaction).
- Devices occasionally show a mid-boot MAC change (kernel log above) which triggers a second DHCP handshake; provisioning agent appears sensitive to transient link resets and can mark network 'unavailable' even after lease is re-established.
comments: 2026-03-08 13:02 - Oscar Ruiz: Initial triage - confirmed 6 reported devices in inventory. Captured pcap at on-prem switch; seeing DHCP ACKs but inconsistent ARP resolution during the boot window.

2026-03-08 15:45 - SRE Team (via #support): DHCP server shows both old and new MACs leased in the same scope for 3 of the units. We purged stale leases for one device (asset TAG RWD-2051) and repro attempt progressed to SCEP successfully.
2026-03-09 09:14 - Depot Ops (J. Patel): Noted we update EC firmware as part of NVMe replacement workflow. Will suspend EC firmware flash for next 10 devices for A/B test.

2026-03-10 11:22 - Oscar Ruiz: Applied temporary workaround script to provisioning image that forces dhclient release/renew on link change and waits for successful TCP handshake to scep endpoint before proceeding. Patch PR created: https://github.com/redwood/infrastructure/pull/2387
2026-03-11 17:03 - QA (L. Park): Deployed patched image to staging depot; 0/12 failures in reproduced runs (was 4/12 previously).
2026-03-13 08:47 - Maya Chen: Marking as resolved after coordination with Depot Ops and SRE. Follow-ups assigned for automation and upstream fixes.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: EC firmware flash during depot repair transiently resets NIC or swaps MAC presented to kernel, creating a race where provisioning-agent believes network unavailable while DHCP server still holds stale binding. Evidence: kernel log shows MAC change mid-boot and DHCP server shows duplicate/stale leases. Reproduced by forcing a NIC reset mid-provision; provisioning-agent reliably failed unless DHCP lease was purged or provisioning image waited for stable TCP connect to SCEP. SRE confirmed DHCP behavior; purging lease allowed normal flow. Patch approach: ensure provisioning flow treats transient link drops as recoverable by explicitly releasing and renewing DHCP and validating TCP reachability to SCEP before marking network as 'ready'.
resolution:
Temporary workaround: updated provisioning image (v2026-03-10-hotfix) with a pre-provision network-stabilizer script that: (1) on link state change runs dhclient -r && dhclient, (2) retries TCP connect to scep.redwood.internal up to 10 times with backoff, (3) delays provisioning-agent start until network check passes. Deployed to production depot image and applied to the 6 affected units (remote DHCP lease purge by SRE + reimage). Result: all 6 devices enrolled successfully.

Long-term action items (follow-up tickets created):
- DEVOPS-434: Add a hardware-level check to depot SOP to skip EC firmware flash when unnecessary and log prior MACs.
- SRE-389: Add DHCP server routine to detect duplicate leases and auto-surge purge stale bindings for depot scope.
- INFRA-PR-2387: Merge provisioning network-stabilizer script into main image builder (PR created).

Workaround time per device: ~30 minutes. No data loss. Customer impact limited to device turnaround time.
next_steps: 1) Merge PR and bake new image into depot pipeline (owner: Oscar Ruiz). 2) Depot Ops to run 100-device A/B test to confirm EC flash correlation (owner: J. Patel). 3) SRE to add DHCP lease collision alerting for depot scope (owner: SRE team).
